title: Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node
hints: 'next node on the same level' is exactly the node processed right after this one in a left-to-right level order traversal, within the same level
process the queue one level at a time; as you pop nodes off in order, each node's next is simply the node you pop right after it - except for the last one in the level
write the CURRENT node's answer into the output array using the VALUE of the node you just popped after it (or -1 if this was the last pop of the level)
make sure to initialize every output position to -101 first, so sentinel/missing positions are correctly left untouched
commonMistakes: linking a node to the first node of the NEXT level instead of correctly assigning -1 to the last node of the current level
forgetting to leave sentinel/out-of-bounds positions as -101 in the output, overwriting them with garbage
using the node's own array position to decide 'rightmost' instead of tracking level membership, which breaks when there are sentinel gaps between real siblings

content.problemStatement:
A binary tree is given as a plain integer array named `tree`, using a complete-binary-tree (heap) index layout:

- the root sits at index 0
- a node at index `i` has its left child at index `2*i+1` and right child at index `2*i+2`
- a child index only counts as real if it's within the array bounds **and** its value isn't the sentinel `-101`
- `-101` means "no node here" - real node values always fall between -100 and 100, so -101 can never be a genuine value

For example, `[1, 2, 3, -101, 4]` encodes this tree:

```
      1
     / \
    2   3
     \
      4
```

Node 2 has no left child (sentinel) but does have a right child, 4.

**Connect every node to the node immediately to its right on the same level, the way you would connect siblings across a level with "next" pointers, and build and return a new array with the exact same shape (same length, same positions) as `tree`, where each position that held a real node now holds the value of the next node to its right on the same level, or -1 if that node is the rightmost one on its level.**

Positions that were sentinel or missing in the input should stay exactly -101 in the output, they have no node, so nothing to connect.
constraints: every real node value is in the range -100 to 100
the sentinel value -101 marks a missing node and never appears as a real value
the output array has exactly the same length and shape as the input
notes: a tree where every level has exactly one node (a chain), so every real position becomes -1
a tree with sentinel gaps between real nodes on the same level, where the next-right connection has to skip over the gap

optimal.space: O(n) for the queue and output array
optimal.pattern: BFS with a queue, processing one level at a time and linking each node to the next one popped in the same round

bruteForce.approach: recursive DFS collecting node indices grouped by depth, then a second pass linking each group's consecutive values and writing -1 for the last one
bruteForce.space: O(n) for the grouped indices, plus O(h) recursion stack
